y1: The disciples asked, “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Jesus called a little child and had him stand among them.
y2: “Unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.”
y3: The shepherd looking for the lost sheep
y4: “If a shepherd has a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders away, he leaves the ninety-nine and goes to look for the one that wandered off.”
y5: “And if he finds it, he is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander off. In the same way, your Father in heaven does not want any of these little ones to be lost.”
y7: Peter asked, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my friend when he sins against me? Up to seven times?”
y8: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times.” This means to forgive without counting.
y10: A servant owed the king a huge debt he could not pay. When the servant begged, the king took pity on him and canceled the whole debt.
y11: But that servant went out, grabbed his fellow servant who owed him very little, and threw him into prison. The king was angry: “Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?”
verse: “Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.”
prayer: Dear God, thank You for looking for me and rejoicing when I was like a lost sheep. Help me to be humble like a child. Just as You forgave me a huge debt, help me to forgive my friend. I pray in Jesus Christ's name. Amen.
d0: great. Being the most important and high. In the kingdom of heaven, a humble person is great. Whoever humbles himself is the greatest.
d1: shepherd. A person who cares for and protects sheep. The shepherd went to look for the lost sheep.
d2: lose. When something you have goes missing. God does not want anyone to be lost.
d3: forgive. To accept someone who made a mistake without blaming them anymore. Forgive seventy-seven times.
d4: debt. Money that is borrowed and must be paid back. The king canceled the servant's entire debt.
